newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures mixed in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures mixed in thin volume.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading mixed in thin volume with September California Oregon Border (COB) taking some strength from hydroelectric generation cutbacks, industry sources said.

As of 1305 EDT, September COB was trading up 31 cents at the day's high of $22.40 following exchange as low as $21.70, while October COB was down five cents at the day's high of $21.15 following trade as low as $21.00 per megawatt hour (MWh).

September COB was reported to be taking some strength from news that three power turbines, with a total capacity of 1,425 megawatts (MW), at the Grand Coulee hydropower dam in Washington state were off line as of early Friday.
The dam's 600 MW unit 21 was restarted Thursday, but was taken back down for adjustments. Unit 21 has been down for scheduled maintenance since February, but is expected back later today.

The 700 MW Grand Coulee turbine 23 was also taken off-line Thursday and will be out of operation through year-end for planned maintenance. In addition, the dam's 125 MW unit 16 is also off line for standard maintenance, and is expected to restart sometime later this month.
Grand Coulee has a total rated capacity of 6,150 MW.

Also as of 1305 EDT, September Palo Verde (PV) was trading down 13 cents at the day's high of $28.50 after reaching as low as $28.05, while October was trading steady at $21.95 following exchanges in a range of $21.70-22.00 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1225 EDT an estimated total of 189 PV and 60 COB contracts had traded.
Separately, the 750 MW unit 5 at the Four Corners coal-fired power complex in New Mexico was expected to restart Sunday after being shut earlier this month for repairs.
The 254 MW unit 1 at the Valmy coal-fired power plant in Nevada was expected to restart Sunday or Monday after being shut earlier this week due to a rotor problem.

In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to be near-normal over the weekend and then cooling to one to five degrees Fahrenheit below normal by the end of the weekend and into early next week, Weather Services Corp said.
In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to be near-normal into early next week, with possible temperatures slightly below normal in the south.
Transmission capacity on the Pacific Intertie, which links the Pacific Northwest to Southern Califoria, remained at 6,300 MW pending final approval of system operating procedures.
Once those are cleared, which is expected to happen by Monday, the rating will be lifted to 6,900 MW.
